text:
deploy-bot: CI perf job staging-canary/l7 reported spike in end-to-end SSE latencies on nightly runs, 95p ~2.7x vs baseline. tagging eng-runtime and infra.
lee: :eyes: saw the alert, pausing canary rollout. any obvious recent merges?
maya: rolling deploy started 3 hours ago, included PR #5123 (rlib: coalesce-sse-writes) and #5140 (toolcall: handshake refactor).
jon: i repro locally with the stress harness — small messages (sub-1kb) get delayed ~150-300ms before first byte. big messages unaffected. looks like write batching delay.
maya: reproducer (from jon):
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" http://staging-inference.local/stream?model=fast
# request payload triggers tool-call path
```
jon: when toolcall path is enabled, we see more syscalls and fragmented writes. pprof shows time blocked in runtime.flushScheduler and net/http.(*conn).writeLoop.
lee: piqued suspicion around the coalesce change — it added a small write timer to accumulate writes for 5-10ms to reduce syscalls. maybe it backfired on SSE where low-latency single-token writes are expected.
maya: adding profiling snippets: flamegraph hotspots (simplified):
```
flushScheduler 45%
serializeToolCall 25%
net.writeLoop 20%
user-space-timer:coalesce 8%
```
priya: interesting: KV cache hits drop too for these traces when toolcall enabled. toolcall serializes a wrapper proto then triggers prefix mismatch so cache keys don't match, causing extra work.
jon: dug into the diff: #5123 introduced per-connection coalesce timer and moved small-write batching to user-space timer; #5140 changed toolcall handshake to insert a small JSON header before proto. together they create many tiny writes separated by timer boundary.
lee: so two orthogonal changes interacting — classic. can we bisect to a single commit causing measurable regression?
maya: ran bisect across the release window: commit a1f3d4 (coalesce initial) increases median by 10ms; commit b2e6ff (toolcall header) adds another 120ms tail on SSE with toolcall. both needed to produce the 2.7x number.
sre-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026, high SSE latency on canary, partition: toolcall + small-write coalesce.
jon: quick patch idea: skip coalesce timer for persistent event-stream routes (Content-Type: text/event-stream || EventStream flag). i can prototype.
priya: alternative is to make toolcall handshake write atomic (single writev) so coalesce doesn't observe two separate writes. that might be lower-risk.
lee: CI perf job failed too — we should pin canary and revert the lower-risk change. which is safer to revert? the coalesce change had perf benefits for bursty RPCs. toolcall header change was for schema normalization but we can delay.
maya: i prefer reverting toolcall header change in canary to restore SSE latencies, keep coalesce. fewer regressions to other paths.
jon: i pushed a quick revert PR: #5152 (revert: toolcall handshake header). running canary smoke now.
lee: thanks. also add a unit test that simulates SSE with toolcall on small writes to catch regressions in CI.
maya: test idea: harness sends 50 small messages and asserts p50/p95 < 40ms. will add to integration-perf suite.
sre-bot: canary smoke results: after revert, 95p back to baseline on staging-canary (run 2026-03-18T10:12Z). reopening rollout after manual verification.
priya: follow-up: still want a long-term fix: either coalesce needs route-aware bypass, or toolcall handshake should use a single write. we'll schedule a backport and a proper patch.
lee: filing tech-debt task and tagging in sprint. thanks all for fast bisect. :thumbsup:
maya: note for postmortem: interaction of user-space write batching with protocol-level multi-write handshakes. add to postmortems/SEV-triage.
jon: leaving logs and pprof capture at http://artifacts.internal/2065432100/sse-bisect/ (permissions internal).
deploy-bot: rollout unpaused for canary after verification. release-manager notified.
